svg.title: The floppy infant: stabilize an unstable infant with ABCDE first, confirm low tone with the suspension and pull-to-sit tests, then sort central from peripheral hypotonia by consciousness, development, strength and reflexes; each column gives its causes, investigations, and shared treatment by referral and supportive care

svg.text: hypotonia = less resistance to PASSIVE stretch · NOT the same as weakness

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Dextrose: check glucose, treat hypoglycemia NOW · Expose: injury or bleeding

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: acute onset: most often INFECTION · always consider non-accidental trauma

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Stable: confirm LOW TONE, then CENTRAL or PERIPHERAL?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: vertical suspension: slips through your hands · horizontal: drapes in a U

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: pull to sit: big head lag (normal head lag gone by 2-6 months)
